content.title: Brock Lesnar Retirement: Why Brock Lesnar Retired At Wrestlemania 42 After Losing Match To Oba Femi?
content.text: Brock Lesnar retirement Wrestlemania 42: Did Brock Lesnar retire at Wrestlemania 42? This is the question on everyone's minds. The Beast, who competed in the opening match of WrestleMania 2026 Night 2, trended on social media as he dropped a major hint about retiring from WWE. Discover moreSports NewsWorld Wrestling Entertainment (WWE)TV Shows & ProgramsMovieCelebritymovies Why Brock Lesnar Retired At Wrestlemania 42? In an interesting development, Oba Femi defeated Brock Lesnar in the first match of WM 2 Night 2, setting the tone for the event. He secured an easy victory over the former WWE Champion, making his Wrestlemania debut in style. After losing the match to Oba, Brock hung up his boots, confirming that he is retiring from active in-ring competition. He left his boots and gloves in the middle of ring as he got emotional. Paul Heyman, who was by his side, broke down into tears as Brock left the ring. The crowd chanted 'Thank you Brock', giving us a memorable moment at WM 2026 in Las Vegas. Full Results, Highlights WWE Wrestlemania 42 night 2 delivered six matches, major title changes and some quick finishes. Roman Reigns, Rhea Ripley and Trick Williams all left with singles championships. Oba Femi scored a rapid win over Brock Lesnar, while “The Demon” Finn Bálor overcomes Dominik Mysterio in a Street Fight. The World Heavyweight Championship main event saw Roman Reigns defeat CM Punk by pinfall in a singles bout that lasts 33:56. Earlier, Rhea Ripley beat Jade Cargill, ending Cargill’s WWE Women's Championship reign after 10:08. Trick Williams, accompanied by Lil Yachty, pinned Sami Zayn in 7:07 to capture the WWE United States Championship. WWE Wrestlemania 42 results full card Penta retained the WWE Intercontinental Championship in a six-pack ladder match lasting 15:08. Penta defeats Je'Von Evans, Dragon Lee, JD McDonagh, Rusev and Rey Mysterio by climbing and retrieving the title. “The Demon” Finn Bálor overcame Dominik Mysterio by pinfall in a 10:27 Street Fight, adding another decisive result to the show. The opening singles contest ended quickly as Oba Femi pinned Brock Lesnar in 4:46, despite Paul Heyman’s presence at ringside. Across the card, every championship match featured a clear pinfall or ladder victory, giving Wrestlemania 42 Night 2 a straightforward results sheet with no disqualifications or count-out finishes.
